title.narrative: Policies and strategies adopted and actional programmes implemented for inclusive skills training and lifelong learning providing equal opportunities for vulnerable groups

description.narrative:
China is advancing towards a responsive, inclusive, and sustainable labour market by promoting lifelong skills development for all and stable employment for 1.25 million people living with HIV (PLHIV) and empowering 85 million persons with disabilities. The labour market is rapidly transitioning due to technological and green transformations, requiring effective skills acquisition, upskilling, and reskilling for 740 million workers. However, ineffective cooperation between employers and training providers leads to skill mismatches, undermining productivity and employment quality. Specific policy measures, especially on green and digital skills, are needed.
Government-led initiatives like the 14th Five-Year Plan on Vocational Training, National ‘Skills China’ Action Plan, and the Three-Year Action Plan to Promote Employment for People with Disabilities, along with commitments from multinational corporations, are driving progress. The ILO collaborates with national stakeholders to strengthen lifelong skills development, drive equitable economic growth, and enhance social inclusion. The ILO works with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) and social partners on a PPP project for quality apprenticeships and lifelong learning, aiming to boost employability in the digital and green transition. Partnerships with UNAIDS, UNESCO, UNFPA, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS), China Disabled Persons’ Federation, and community organizations expand job opportunities for PLHIV and persons with disabilities.
The Country Outcome Programme CHN251 focuses on providing policy advice, developing guides and tools for digital and green skills, enhancing understanding of HIV and disability issues, integrating international best practices, conducting technical capacity building, and empowering vulnerable groups through targeted skills training programs.
